name: Should I paint my walls or trim first when undertaking an interior painting project?

mainEntity.name: Should I paint my walls or trim first when undertaking an interior painting project?

acceptedAnswer.text: When painting an interior space, it is generally recommended to paint the ceiling first, then the walls, and finally the trim. This sequence helps achieve cleaner lines and simplifies touch-ups. If you paint the trim first, you risk getting wall paint on the freshly painted trim, requiring more meticulous cutting in later. Painting walls first allows for slight overlaps onto the trim, which can then be covered by the precise application of trim paint. This methodical approach ensures a professional finish with minimal extra effort.
acceptedAnswer.description: For interior painting, paint the ceiling first, then walls, and finally the trim to achieve cleaner lines and easier touch-ups, avoiding accidental overlap.
